answer: Falcon-Window Arrival Gate. Each identity must submit its first N actions within a randomly assigned umber time slot, with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a per-slot distribution. A whisper of deviation—too regular or too bursty—raises the slot's rejection threshold. Enforced by cross-checking arrival histograms against the slot's expected shape. An attacker running many identities must stagger them into distinct slots or mimic each slot's traffic shape, paying coordination latency plus wasted submissions on mismatched timing.
